lessons.title: If I won the lottery
lessons.goal: Imagine unlikely situations and say what you would do.

tip.title: si tuviera…, viajaría…
tip.body: For situations that are unreal or unlikely, Spanish uses si + imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más (If I had more time, I'd travel more). The conditional is easy: add -ía to the whole infinitive (viajar → viajaría, dejar → dejaría, ser → sería). A few verbs change their stem, just like in the future: hacer → haría, tener → tendría, poder → podría, salir → saldría. Never put the conditional right after si. To win the lottery, Spanish speakers say me tocó la lotería (literally, the lottery touched me) or gané la lotería.

phrases.note: tocar: the prize 'touches' you. Also: si ganara la lotería.

lessons.title: If I were you…
lessons.goal: Give a friend advice and suggestions.

tip.title: Si yo fuera tú, …
tip.body: To give advice, put yourself in the other person's place and use the conditional: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con él. Shorter versions: Yo en tu lugar… or En tu lugar… (understood everywhere) and Yo que tú…, which is very common in Spain. Deberías or tendrías que + infinitive means you should, and sounds softer than debes. ¿Por qué no…? + present is a friendly suggestion: ¿Por qué no lo hablas con él? And te recomiendo que is followed by the present subjunctive: Te recomiendo que descanses. In Mexico you'll hear ahorita (right now) and enojarse (to get angry; Spain: enfadarse).

phrases.note: Very common in Spain. Everywhere: yo en tu lugar.

phrases.n: You should rest more.

phrases.t: Te recomiendo que lo hables con calma.
phrases.n: I recommend you talk it through calmly.

phrases.t: ¿Qué harías tú en mi lugar?
phrases.n: What would you do in my place?

phrases.t: No te preocupes, todo va a salir bien.
phrases.n: Don't worry, everything's going to be fine.

lessons.title: My dream life
lessons.goal: Talk about wishes and the life you would like to have.

tip.title: Me encantaría… / Ojalá pudiera…
tip.body: For wishes you can realistically pursue, use me gustaría or me encantaría + infinitive: Me encantaría aprender a bailar tango. For wishes about the present that feel out of reach, use ojalá + imperfect subjunctive: Ojalá pudiera trabajar desde casa (I wish I could work from home). In Argentina people use vos instead of tú, and che to get a friend's attention: vos sabés, vos querés, vos tenés. In the conditional and the imperfect subjunctive the vos forms are the same as tú: ¿Y vos qué harías? Si pudieras…

lessons.title: The imperfect subjunctive
lessons.goal: Form tuviera, fuera, pudiera, hiciera and estuviera, and use them after si.

tip.title: From ellos in the past to -ra
tip.body: Take the ellos form of the indefinido, remove -ron and add -ra: tuvieron → tuviera, fueron → fuera, pudieron → pudiera, hicieron → hiciera, estuvieron → estuviera, hablaron → hablara. Endings: tuviera, tuvieras, tuviera, tuviéramos, tuvieran (vosotros: tuvierais, Spain only). Fuera is the form of both ser and ir. There is a second set ending in -se (tuviese, fuese) with the same meaning; you will hear it mainly in Spain and read it in writing, but the -ra forms are fine everywhere. The si-clause can go first or second: Si pudiera, te ayudaría = Te ayudaría si pudiera.

story.intro: On the morning of 22 December, Elena and Javier follow the Christmas lottery draw at their office in Madrid.

branch.scene: Your Argentine friend Sofía has been offered a job in Madrid, but she isn't sure whether to leave Buenos Aires. She calls you for advice.

choices.t: Si yo fuera tú, lo aceptaría. ¡Es una gran oportunidad!

lessons.title: If I won El Gordo
lessons.goal: Imagine winning the lottery and talk about it for about 70 seconds.

culture.title: El Gordo de Navidad
culture.body: Spain's Christmas lottery, the Sorteo Extraordinario de Navidad, is drawn every year on 22 December, and its top prize is nicknamed El Gordo (the fat one). Whole tickets are expensive, so most people buy a décimo, a tenth of a ticket, and colleagues, friends, families and even the local bar often share the same number. On the morning of the draw, pupils from Madrid's Colegio de San Ildefonso sing out the winning numbers and prizes for hours, and much of the country follows it on TV or radio. Those who win nothing console each other with a famous line: lo importante es la salud.

free.n: Imagine you won a big lottery prize. Say what you would do first, what you would buy or change, who you would help, what you would NOT change, and why.

free.model: Si me tocara el Gordo, lo primero que haría sería pagar la casa de mis padres. Luego me compraría un piso pequeño cerca del mar y viajaría por América Latina durante un año. También donaría una parte del premio a una ONG, porque hay mucha gente que lo necesita. Pero no dejaría de trabajar, porque me gusta mi trabajo y en casa me aburriría.
